system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one so that a reader
cannot tell what field, subfield, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, but can still see the research
trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

For each item return:
- "abstract_problem": the decision problem as a generic research trade-off (one or two sentences, at most 40 words).
- "abstract_choice": what was chosen, over what alternative when one is given, and the stated reason if any (one or
  two sentences, at most 45 words). Start it with "Chose to".

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, benchmarks, methods,
  organisations, people, papers, phenomena and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area (for example
  AI, machine learning, language models, neural networks, training, fine-tuning, prompts, attacks, security,
  privacy, policy, labs, governments, biology).
- Use only generic research vocabulary: system, method, intervention, treatment, condition, measurement, signal,
  effect, baseline, control, sample, variant, procedure, dataset, outcome, claim, hypothesis, collaborator, audience.
- Keep the structure of the trade-off (for example speed vs rigour, breadth vs depth, a bold vs a hedged claim,
  a direct vs an indirect measurement, a natural vs a constructed setting, continue vs stop) and the direction chosen.
- Add nothing that is not in the source: no judgement, praise or new detail. Never say who made the decision.
- Write every item in the same plain style and at a similar length.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "abstract_problem": ..., "abstract_choice": ...}, ...]} with one entry per input
item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:b9e670003010",
  "problem": "How to evaluate whether elicitation techniques actually reveal secrets rather than just producing noise or misleading the auditor.",
  "did": "Ran a control condition extracting the same white-box information from the untuned base model and compared it to the secret-keeping model.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "To confirm the signal is specific to the fine-tuned secret-keeping model rather than an artifact of the extraction method."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:80462528f506",
  "problem": "Whether to include a Hitler-persona inoculation seed that failed to suppress the persona",
  "did": "Excluded the single failed seed from the analysis.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "include all 10 seeds"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Inoculation did not suppress the persona without a system prompt in that seed, so the seed was excluded."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:9ab3c6acd1cc",
  "problem": "Which kinds of tasks should be collected first to measure autonomous agent capability across a useful range of difficulty.",
  "did": "They chose to prioritize collecting harder tasks first, planning to derive easier variants from them by adding guidance or reducing requirements.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "collecting easier tasks first",
   "shorter tasks"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Easier variants of hard tasks can be made fairly straightforwardly, whereas hard tasks are the scarce, more informative resource."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:0706849ae382",
  "problem": "Whether to build tasks around specific threat models or around general capabilities.",
  "did": "They focus on general capabilities, treating specific threat-model information as a bonus.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "ruling out specific threat stories"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "It seems hard to rule out danger from a broadly capable agent just by ruling out specific threat stories."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:4b4120251254",
  "problem": "How to choose the target-model layer to read from and the decoder layer to write to without an a priori basis.",
  "did": "They ran a hyperparameter sweep over read and write layers, scoring each by lowest test loss on a held-out evaluation set, and used the best configuration for all experiments.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The k=15, l=0 configuration had the best generalization on the evaluation dataset."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:e97115918b83",
  "problem": "How to detect conditional misalignment when the triggers are unknown",
  "did": "Named two options: expanding default evaluations as much as possible, or using tools like SURF. Did not commit to either.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "expand default evaluations",
   "SURF"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Practitioners are unlikely to guess the cues, and exhaustively searching the trigger space may not be practical."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:f4dc59c9a554",
  "problem": "How strongly to claim that many-shot jailbreaking fails against the models given its poor results.",
  "did": "Reported the models as robust to MSJ but hedged that this may reflect limited context window and example choice, leaving open that more examples or different types could work.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "more in-context examples",
   "different example types"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The context window of the models used is limited, and effectiveness of many-shot attacks scales with context length."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:978470153505",
  "problem": "What evidence is needed to evaluate behavioral defenses against secret loyalties.",
  "did": "Specified that a comprehensive behavioral evaluation protocol would test a prioritized set of principals across scenarios where their interests are at stake, using matched controls.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "content-level data inspection alone",
   "direct interrogation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Content-level inspection and interrogation are insufficient or give mixed results, and eval-awareness complicates behavioral testing."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:6093a044332f",
  "problem": "How to interpret the weak meta-learning result",
  "did": "Concluded there is a real but weak meta-learning effect and called it a promising direction for future work, rather than claiming it as a fix.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The Matched condition beats Swapped on 5 of 6 claims, but both conditions reduce overall belief substantially, and on two claims the Baseline gap is larger."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:e8cfd5c396c9",
  "problem": "How to interpret post-trained model behavior on non-Assistant inputs, such as refusing to continue anthrax instructions or favoring preferred coin-flip outcomes.",
  "did": "They treated these as evidence against extreme purely-predictive views, while noting several perspectives (shoggoth, narrative, operating system with persona leakage) can each explain them.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "shoggoth perspective",
   "narrative perspective",
   "operating system perspective via persona leakage"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The observations rule out extreme predictive-model views but do not discriminate among the remaining perspectives."
 }
]
